publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A visual sense system for robots which can measure and recognize 3-D objects is proposed. This robot vision system is capable of recognizing machine parts moving on a line so that an automated transferring and assembly system with high flexibility and no dependence on external peripheral equipment can be realized. This system possesses two remarkable features. One is the measuring technique, which can effectively remove the false 3-D information due to mirror reflection using laser slit beams from two directions. The other is the technique of carrying out the recognition of polygonal surfaces by p-type Fourier descriptor, area and perimeter, and, further, the recognition of objects based on aspect graphs, using multistage neural networks. As compared with the conventional recognition method, the speed and accuracy of recognition rose a step.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of atmospheric effect on the emergent radiation over non-uniform terrain
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: For precise atmospheric correction over nonuniform terrain in satellite imagery, a numerical method for evaluating the upwelling radiation at the top of the atmosphere bounded by a nonuniform surface is developed. This method makes it possible to treat quantitatively the case of a hazy atmosphere and/or the large albedo of the surface. The present version is basically an extension of a one-dimensional radiative transfer code, so that it is very economical in terms of computer time. Thus, it would be suitable for simulating the satellite imagery.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A composition of the neural network using switched-capacitor circuit
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A switched-capacitor (SC) neural network is described. The motion of the SC neural network is represented with stochastic difference equations. The network consists of two-state neurons (ON-OFF neurons). The equations can lead to a convergence to global minima even with the two-state neurons by introducing the technique of simulated annealing. The two-state neurons make the circuits of the activation function and multiplication very simple. The network limitation of the SC neural network is analyzed in detail, and the circuit performance of 32.8 GCPS is confirmed. The computational capacity of the SC neural network is confirmed in connection with the solution of an optimization problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On numerically robust adaptive recursive filters
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The author treats some aspects of numerical robustness of adaptive recursive filters, i.e., adaptive filters whose programmable filters are recursive. Attention is given to the enhancement of numerical robustness and stability monitoring.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analog VLSI edge detection chip and digital multiprocessor chip for neural-based vision processing
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A mixed-signal VLSI design for early vision processing, which includes an analog edge detection chip with embedded array photosensors and a digital multiprocessor chip, is described. The system architecture overview shows that the combination of the analog chip and the digital processors can perform highly efficient processing in neural-based vision processing. The analog edge detection chip consisting of 258*258 photosensor cells can be implemented in an area of 13.5 mm*15.5 mm using the MOSIS 0.8- mu m CMOS technology. The digital multiprocessor chip, which includes 64 processing elements, can be implemented in a 15.0-mm*18.0-mm chip using an industrial-scale 0.5- mu m CMOS technology. A system implementation for fingerprint verification is presented as an example of possible applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Grinding robot system with master slave control
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors present a novel grinding robot system with master-slave control in order to use the industrial robot system effectively, in which conventionally the point-to-point teaching playback control is applied. The configuration of the proposed robot system is discussed, and the trajectory tracking performance characteristics are examined. As a result, it is clarified that the industrial robot system with master-slave control can be made useful by adding an interface unit as an intelligent terminal, which connects the industrial robot with the master arm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Haemodynamic trend detection using the median filter
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: Attention is given to methods to obtain clinically useful trend data from invasively monitored haemodynamic parameters in an intensive care unit. The requirements for a trend detector in the context of intensive care are defined. A median filter-based trend detector designed to perform as a preprocessor for a highly specific knowledge-based alarm system is presented. The trend detector uses the standard median filter to preprocess the data before estimating first-order trends with least squares sum line fitting. The detector's responses to artifact input and its reliability as well as its clinical evaluation are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stabilization of large-scale systems by reduced order controllers
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: It is demonstrated that a reduced-order controller that uses the state of a reduced-order model of the original system for feedback purposes can stabilize the original system if a certain condition is satisfied. In the approach to deriving the condition, it is assumed that the nondominant part of the original system may be linearly approximated by the dominant part. The approach taken for the derivation of these conditions is based on the identification and partition of the slow and fast parts of the original system. A Lyapunov function for the original system is formed as a linear combination of the states of the original system which are associated with the slow and fast parts. The fast mode of the system is then approximated in terms of the slower one. As a result, a modified Lyapunov function is obtained from which the condition for global stability is derived. An example is given to illustrate the approach used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Active vibration control for flexible cantilever beam subject to seismic disturbance
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A method of vibration control for a flexible structure modeled by a cantilever beam subject to distributed random disturbance and seismic input at the clamped end is presented. The mathematical model of the flexible cantilever is described by the Euler-Bernoulli-type stochastic partial differential equation including internal damping and the seismic and distributed random forcing terms. The seismic disturbance can be observed with an accelerometer at the clamped end. The controller is obtained by using the stochastic optimal control theory. Simulation studies show that the proposed control method is effective in suppressing random vibration due to random disturbances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architecture of a high-speed hierarchical structure transversal filter
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: An architecture of a high-speed linear phase finite impulse response (FIR) filter is described. This filter can provide an output equivalent to that of a higher-order FIR digital filter due to using a number of lower-order linear phase cascaded integrator comb subfilters or linear phase cascaded differential comb subfilters. It is shown that the design of the filter can be replaced with that of a simple subfilter by using a multiple mapping function. Thus, it is considered that the proposed architecture has the potential to make the design of a higher-order FIR filter easy. As an example, this filter, equivalent to a conventional linear phase FIR filter with about 11-45 filter lengths, has been designed and implemented into an LSI. The realized filter has a maximum sampling rate of 15 MHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Filtering and modeling using covariance information in linear continuous systems
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: Filtering and modeling procedures using covariance information are proposed. The sequential algorithms for the filtering estimate of x(t) from the Wiener-Hopf integral equation are presented based on innovations theory. A numerical simulation result shows that the present algorithms are quite feasible in linear continuous stochastic systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A transcutaneous energy transmission system for an artificial organ by using a novel resonant converter
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A zero voltage switched resonant converter has been designed and built as a transcutaneous energy transmission system to transfer 30 W across a variable air gap of 5-20 mm. The converter could power a total implantable artificial heart through intact skin by utilizing a transformer. In the converter, the large leakage inductances of the transcutaneous transformer have been incorporated in the resonant inductor. The steady-state operation of an experimental transcutaneous power supply has been accurately predicted by the theoretical analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bounded real extension of the Schur-Cohn test
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The importance of reinterpreting the Schur-Cohn test as a lossless bounded realness criterion for rational transfer functions on the unit disk is discussed, and a concept of their lossless bounded real (LBR) realization is introduced. A LBR realizability condition is shown to be equivalent to a lossless bounded realness criterion and then is extended to a bounded real one, which will play a crucial role not only in the realization problem, but also in the inverse scattering problem, digital filter design, and numerical analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new robust stability criterion for interval time-delay systems
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: By using some properties of matrix measures and the matrix's spectral radius, a new stability criterion of a linear time-delay system is derived. This result is also extended to the interval time-delay system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Noniterative real-time design of selective linear phase filters
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A novel approach for designing and realizing variable linear phase finite impulse response (FIR) filters is presented. The proposed filter structure is a cascade of a prefilter and corrector. The author concentrates on selective and computationally efficient filter structures exploiting the generalized recursive running sums (GRRSs) as prefilters. The proposed analytical window design method for the selective filter structures is very simple and fast and it can be implemented easily in hardware or software. The resulting linear phase filters exploiting the GRRSs were superior to the corresponding optimum direct from FIR designs having the same specifications in terms of additions and multiplications per sample.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two-dimensional spectral estimation method with input-dependent FIR prefiltering
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: An approach to 2-D spectral estimation that involves input-dependent finite impulse response (FIR) prefiltering is proposed. This approach is an iterative method in which the design of a 2-D zero-phase FIR filter and the operation of spectral estimation are sequentially performed. Although the authors use the periodogram for the purpose of calculating the power spectrum, an introduction of the input-independent prefiltering leads to high spectral resolvability and reduced estimation variance. The computational time wasted on this approach is moderate, since one can iteratively utilize the computational efficiency of the 2-D fast Fourier transform algorithm. The effectiveness of the spectral estimation method is shown by computer simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A neural network hardware model for image thinning
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors propose a simple 5*5 cloning template of a cellular neural network for imaging thinning. The principle of the template design and hardware model are considered. Although the connected weights between the neurons are asymmetric, it is shown that the network is stable, and it can be easily realized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust flight control using parameterized compensator
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors outline a design method for achieving the desired robustness and performance requirements of a flight control system. By using the U-parameter robust compensator design method, the compensator and the closed-loop transfer function can be formulated with free parameters, Moreover, based on a model reference approach, a simple method is introduced to minimize the H/sup 2/-norm of the error between the designed closed-loop transfer function and the reference model to determine the free parameters of the compensator such that the desired robustness and performance requirements can both be met. Simulation results show that the proposed method can achieve good robustness and performance for the flight control system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A robust tracking control scheme for robotic manipulators with uncertain dynamics
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A variable-structure compensator is designed for the closed-loop feedback control system of a robotic manipulator with uncertain dynamics. It is shown that the closed-loop system with a variable-structure compensator not only behaves with a strong robustness property with respect to large uncertain dynamics, but also makes the output tracking error converge to zero asymptotically.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low complexity decoding for convolutional codes
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: Several attempts to reduce the decoding complexity for convolutional codes are described. Although most of the attempts were unsuccessful, the author gained interesting insight which helped in understanding the theory of convolutional codes and led to further studies. It is concluded that the performance of the standard v=6 Viterbi decoder is hard to beat. The author gives a concatenated coding scheme using the same v=6 code and a distance 2 code to obtain an almost ML decoding algorithm with the performance of a d/sub free/=20 code.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high speed image processor oriented for automated visual inspection system
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A practical computer architecture of a high-speed image processor which has been developed for automated visual inspection systems (AVISs) is presented. It enhances some fundamental functions, aiming at the satisfaction of requirements such as high-speed processing ability, flexibility, and simplicity of system construction. A method of system control by video signal synchronization for the architecture is described, and the realized processor is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Supervised learning in continuous feedback neural network
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: Two supervised learning algorithms for the continuous feedback neural network (CFNN) have been derived which can learn multiple patterns correctly. It is noted that, when the parameters of the CFNN are determined, its dynamic behavior is completely determined, so determining the weight coefficients of the CFNN is a crucial step for using the CFNN. For a CFNN used as associative memory, one wants the required patterns to be the equilibrium points of the CFNN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the discrete-time H/sub infinity / filter via game theoretic approach
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors consider discrete-time H/sub infinity / filters based on a game-theoretic approach. The H/sub infinity / filters are developed based on the discrete-time linear-quadratic (LQ) game. The authors obtain two different filters: a one-step predictor and a filter that yields the current state estimate. It is shown that the steady-state filters exist if an algebraic Riccati equation has a nonnegative solution and that both of the filters satisfy the H/sub infinity / norm bound. The worst disturbance maximizing the energy ratio of the estimation error to the disturbance is also given by linear feedback of the estimation error. Furthermore, the authors propose an H/sub infinity / fixed-lag smoother based on the H/sub infinity / filter derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency-weighting model identification with an adaptive ARMA lattice filter
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A method for model identification with frequency weighting using an adaptive autoregressive moving average (ARMA) lattice filter is proposed. Based on this algorithm, the accuracy of the model identification can be higher in focused frequency bands than in other bands. The proposed algorithm contains two algorithms. One is a realization algorithm of an ARMA lattice filter with frequency weighting. The other is an algorithm which computes ARMA parameters from the coefficients of the ARMA lattice filter. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed filter has low sensitivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel approach of fuzzy control
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors propose a novel fuzzy controller (NFC) based on the application of fuzzy logic. The proposed novel fuzzy controller is designed to achieve better transient response and steady state performance than that of the conventional PI-fuzzy controller and PD-fuzzy controller. Advantage of the NFC is demonstrated by a simulation study.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Engineering drawing recognition based on a line decomposition and re-composition method
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A novel drawing recognition system that works efficiently is presented. The authors introduce a novel representation of input images for drawings with breaks and touching lines. The representation involves both geometric and topological information described in terms of line segments. This representation permits drawing recognition through the processes of primitive decomposition and object extraction. The primitive decomposition process splits every black region in an image into primitive line segments, and generates an intermediate description. Next, the object extraction process groups the primitive lines into such meaningful sets as character strings, symbols, and lines by recognition techniques based on the intermediate description. The proposed technique has been applied to a recognition system for complicated drawings such as equipment diagrams superimposed on a map, and to a system which can extract lines from mechanical drawings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automatic measurement of ship's attitude by the use of servo-type accelerometers
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A ship's attitude measurement system which measures the heaving, rolling, and pitching of a ship is presented. The system has four servo-type accelerometers appropriately located on the ship. By modeling the quantities adequately and using Kalman filters, online measurement of the quantities is realized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new model reference adaptive control law
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A model reference adaptive control mechanism for controlling linear time-varying processes is introduced. In this mechanism, only one controller parameter is adjusted to compensate for variations in the plant parameters while keeping the remaining controller parameters fixed. Online estimation of the process parameters is required to find the values of the adaptive controller parameters, which can be done by allowing one controller parameter to vary while keeping the rest fixed. Then by equating the system difference equation to the model output, one can solve for the adjustable parameter. The closer the estimate of the process parameters to their true values, the closer is the convergence of the system output to that of the model. This method has a very fast convergence rate, because the controller parameter is adjusted online at every sampling instant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interpolatory estimation of multi-dimensional orthogonal expansions with stochastic coefficients
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The interpolation of multidimensional signals is widely considered in connection with the problem of suppressing the immanent redundancy contained in an image without vitiating the quality of the resultant approximation. The minimization of the approximation error is one of the important problems in this field. In the field of information processing, one sometimes considers the orthonormal development of an image each coefficient of which represents the principal feature of the image. The selection of the orthonormal bases becomes important in this problem. Fisher's criterion is a powerful tool for declustering. The combination of these two analyses is an interesting problem in image processing. In the present work, the optimum interpolatory approximation of multidimensional orthogonal expansions is established, and some remarks are made on the above problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and realization of the distributed controller for a fixed topology MIMD computer
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: Some paradigms of the design of a distributed controller for multiple-instruction multiple-data (MIMD) machines have been pointed out, and an asynchronous method for data exchange in a multi-SIMD (single-instruction multiple-data) computer with distributed memory based on data synchronization is addressed, as well as a new implementation method for the exclusive access to a shared resource. A hardware realization of the proposed approach in the binary pyramid SPHINX is given. Limits and possible extensions of the proposed approach are also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modeling and dynamic stabilization for suspension system using tuned LC circuit
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors develop a transfer function model of magnetic suspension systems using a tuned LC circuit by linearizing system equations near the equilibrium state. This model not only explains nicely the inherent dynamic instability but also gives the necessary condition of stability. The authors also present a novel dynamic stabilization method for magnetic suspension systems using a tuned LC circuit. In order to achieve stable suspension without any mechanical contact, damping is applied to the moveable stator rather than to the suspended object directly. Simulations are carried out to confirm the theoretical analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Realization of geometric illusions in human vision with artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A novel physiological model is proposed for the geometrical illusion phenomenon in human vision. This model assumes that the illusion is a result of nonuniform bending in visual space whose Riemannian metric tensor is determined by the excitatory state of the lateral inhibitory neural network. It can be easily implemented by artificial neural networks. The neural network model was used to realize (qualitatively, but it can be fine-tuned) the Ebbinhaus illusion, the Zollner illusion 1, the Hering illusion 2, the Wundt illusion, the Muller-Lyer illusion, the Helmholtz vertical illusion, and the concentric circle illusion, and to settle the notorious paradox of displacement for Hering 7 and the Wundt illusion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Minimizing the energy of active contour by using a Hopfield network
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A Hopfield network for minimizing the constrained energy of an active contour model (snake) is proposed. Taking advantage of the parallel computation and energy convergence capabilities of the Hopfield network, this method is faster and more stable for resolving the boundary locating problem than the conventional methods. The Hopfield network is superior to conventional methods in three ways. First, the Hopfield network can be implemented in a parallel architecture, instead of the sequential process, in real-time application. Second, it guarantees that the energy of the snake can converge to a minimum stable state. Finally, it allows hard constraints to be included as a part of the minimization process. As a result, the present study reveals the possibility that a human vision system can locate an object boundary by using a mechanism similar to the active contour model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of an image processing system for texture segmentation
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The development of a two-level machine vision system for the fast segmentation of textured images. A transputer network was used to realize the upper level, thus providing a powerful, expandable computing platform on which to execute intermediate and high-level vision algorithms. Low-level vision operations were delegated to a custom-developed pipeline card, permitting cost-effective, in-process execution of the required texture segmentation functions. The use of alternative data scans on the pipeline card further reduced hardware costs by allowing the decomposition of large moving average filters into one-dimensional filters performed orthogonally on the data set. This required fewer image processing ICs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Theory of generalized interpolatory approximation of multi-dimensional signals
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A favorable generalized subband approximation for multidimensional signals has been presented by T. Kida and H. Mochizuki (1992). In this result, all the interpolation functions have different functional forms in general. In this paper, initially it is assumed that the interpolation functions have different functional forms. However, the resultant optimum interpolation functions are expressed as the parallel shifts of the finite number of the n-dimensional functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A next generation expert system for flexible assembly
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: An attempt is made to demonstrate the feasibility of an engineering approach to machine learning through the development of a robotic system that learns to perform assembly tasks from clearly specified training instances. A major technological impediment to increasing productivity in the manufacturing sector is the relative absence of automation at most stages of the product design process. One such stage involves the translation of nonprocedural goal files-describing the desired result of some aspect of the manufacturing process-into procedural task files. The task files detail the exact sequence of required steps as typified by an assembly operation. Flexibility is introduced with an expert translator. The technique provides for coordination among the assembly robots and minimizes costly down-time. The system has been implemented in C and is supported by the Sun 3/50 platform. An advanced prototype has been implemented at the Naval Command, Control, and Ocean Surveillance Center on a DAP-610 supercomputer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A canonical design form of two-dimensional digital filters
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors propose a method for obtaining the canonical design form of two-dimensional digital filters (2DDFs). By using this method, design can be directly obtained from the coefficients of the transfer functions of 2DDFs without performing canonical decomposition of the state equations and solving nonlinear equations. The possibility of reducing the design dimension in the canonical design is considered, and conditions imposed on the transfer functions of 2DDFs for the reduction are obtained. Moreover, a class of transfer functions of 2DDFs that can be designed with a minimal dimension with respect to both of two variables is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Retrieval of aerosol profile based on inversion algorithm
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A procedure for estimating the optical thickness and density profile of stratospheric aerosols based on the solar occultation measurement of the Improved Limb Atmospheric Spectrometer (ILAS) is described. The ILAS will be installed on the Advanced Earth Observing Satellite (ADEOS) in 1996. The retrieval algorithm involves vertical structure inversion, which provides the profile of atmospheric extinction from ILAS transmittance data, and the iterative routine in respect of comparison of the simulated results with the measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Toward automation in the optimization of systems models
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors consider large classes of problems in which dynamical systems satisfy nonlinear differential and discrete equations, boundary conditions are to be met, certain functionals are to be minimized or maximized, unknown system parameters are to be identified on the basis of experimental data, and systems are to be designed for optimal utilization, control, and performance. These developments produce rapid prototyping capabilities for systems engineers, systems analysts, software engineers, and others to use in creating intelligent information-based systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault tolerance in neural networks
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: In the hardware realization of neural networks, some physical faults arise during the fabrication that can cause the network to fail. The implementation method will determine the type of fault that will occur. This assertion is examined using a backpropagation (BP) network model for pattern recognition of a subset of the English alphabet, simulated faults in the neurons, and synaptic connections between pairs of neurons. Observing the effects on the system performance when retrieving patterns, it was found that neural networks are tolerant against noise in input pattern and neural networks are tolerant against damage or faults in synaptic links or even neurons. The simulation results showed that, as the probability of damage increases, the network still produces correct results up to a certain limit. This BP model and the Hopfield model were compared for the same application (pattern recognition), which showed that the BP model is better in the sense that the number of nodes is not varied with the number of example patterns as in the case of the Hopfield model.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear filtering without aliasing errors
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A scheme based on a combination of linear and nonlinear filters ensuring high detail-preservation, with no blurring and without giving rise to aliasing artifacts, is described. Nonlinear detail-preserving filters are combined with linear filters using a special frequency detector to switch the operation to a particular filter depending on the local signal content. In signal areas with rapidly varying high-frequency content, the linear filter is switched on to avoid aliasing distortions. In fast-changing signal areas, the nonlinear filter is switched on to avoid blurring edges. The high frequency signal components which may give rise to aliasing errors are effectively removed while edges and details remain intact. Results of tests on real and simulated images indicate that the new scheme unifies the best features of linear and nonlinear filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parameter identification of fluid tubes
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A novel device has been developed which is able to identify the unknown fluid resistance of elastic tubes, such as artificial blood tubes, from the measured water pressures by circulating pulsatile water flow in tubes with a roller pump. The device consists of two pressure sensors, an analog-to-digital transducer board, one roller pump with a constant revolution speed, a lowpass filter to cut off high-frequency noise, and a microcomputer with special software to identify the unknown resistance of the tube. Some experimental results for the identification are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of reflection properties for rugged terrain forests from space
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors introduce a novel analytical correction method for rugged terrain image data which allows the use of the more general Minnaert law for the bidirectional reflection at the ground surface. In this correction model, single reflection by a target slope and multiple reflection by the mean background as well as diffuse reflection by the atmosphere were taken into account. Applying this correction method to Landsat MSS (Multispectral Scanner) data, the authors found that the reflection by rugged terrain vegetation (mostly deciduous forest) follows Minnaert's law rather than Lambert's law.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A modular neural system for handwritten alphabet recognition using invariant moment-based features
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A recognition system for identifying handwritten alphabets using a specific artificial neural network structure is described. Layers of feedforward networks preprocess the alphabets by extracting features that enhance the characters' dissimilarity. The features approximate the moments and moment invariants which are invariant to translation, rotation, and scaling of the processed alphabets. The collective tasks of the feedforward network modules integrate feature extraction preprocessing with classification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of anisotropic structure of myocardium on estimation of ultrasonic tissue parameters
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: When applying ultrasonic tissue characterization to diagnosis of myocardial diseases one must consider the anisotropic characteristics of the myocardium. In the present work, the authors investigated the influence of the orientation of myocardial fibers on the attenuation characteristics of tissues, with the basic experiment using pig myocardium. Some results showed that the value of the attenuation coefficient was greater when the ultrasound beam was directed parallel to the muscle fibers than when it was directed perpendicular to them.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fluctuations on R-R interval time series of diabetic autonomic neuropathy
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: An evaluation of autonomic nervous control using fluctuations of R-R interval variability is presented. Diabetic autonomic neuropathy concerned with autonomic nervous control is discriminated by using the R-R interval time series in the frequency domain. Diabetic autonomic neuropathy has been classified with high recognition employing this method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wideband indoor radio system using orthogonal multicarrier modulation
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors analyze the performance of a multicarrier modulation system with signal transmission during a guard period. They derive the bit error rate (BER) performance of the multicarrier modulation system under time and frequency selective fading environments. The relations between irreducible BER performance and the number of subchannels are shown. Next, they propose a subchannel assignment protocol that provides a variable-bit-rate transmission capability. This protocol provides better packet loss probability and throughput performance than the conventional frequency division multiple access (FDMA) protocol.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuzzy optimal controller design based on neural network for nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A method of constructing a fuzzy optimal controller for nonlinear systems is proposed. The method is based on a fuzzy model and is intended to give optimal control using neural networks. In this method, a cost function is introduced in the neural network, and unsupervised learning is performed. The method is applied numerically to the stabilizing control of a one-machine infinite-bus electric power system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quadratic filters for signal processing: principles and applications
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: An overview of the principles of quadratic filtering and its applications to the processing of 1-D and M-D signals is presented. Two vector notations are introduced to simplify the expressions of the Volterra kernels, and two corresponding efficient realizations are suggested for finite-support 1-D and M-D quadratic filters. Both realizations exhibit properties of modularity and regularity very suitable for VLSI implementations and permit computational and hardware advantages. The linearity of the output of Volterra filters with respect to the kernel elements allows the extension of the theory of the optimum linear filter to the optimum nonlinear Volterra filter, according to the minimum mean-square error criterion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An application of the pseudo boundary of an unstable polytope of polynomials
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors propose a very useful application of the pseudoboundary of an unstable polytope of polynomials by giving a unified procedure to test the stability of uncertain polynomials with multilinear coefficients or even polynomial coefficients in the parameters. In the case when the number of parameters involved in the coefficients of the polynomials is at most three, one can actually partition the parameter space in such a manner that one region gives rise to the stable part and the other the unstable part of the polytope of polynomials. An illustrative example is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust model reference by using modified high gain method
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A novel method for a robust model reference control system is presented. The technique has a very simple structure which implies a low-pass high loop gain, and it can reduce the parameter sensitivity and suppress the external disturbance easily by adjusting some parameters. Computer simulations and experimental results show the good behavior of this technique. The technique has been applied in a hydraulic servo system, and it has been shown to be highly effective and practical.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Relations between sensitivity of moment and root for FIR filters
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The authors propose a method of using the moment of impulse response to evaluate the deviation of frequency characteristic of an finite impulse response (FIR) filter in coefficient quantization. The moment is defined as a weighted summation of impulse responses. The authors develop the moment coefficient sensitivity and discuss how it is related to the zero of FIR filters. Then they propose a new viewpoint which takes the integral of coefficient sensitivity during a period as a measure to evaluate the effect of coefficient quantization and give a simple formula. The benefits of this method are in estimating the peak of deviation of the frequency characteristic and using zeros of the filter only. Furthermore, the measure is used to reconstruct the FIR filter to a two-stage cascade structure with low sensitivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A state estimation method with matching between a physical energy quantity and a decibel scaled noisy observation for a sound environmental system
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A state estimation method for an energy stochastic system with a decibel observation mechanism is presented. The problem is to get a decibel-valued estimate of an energy state variable by using the decibel-valued noisy observation data, where the stochastic system of concern is physically driven on energy scale. The main attention is paid to matching between the physical energy principle and the decibel observation mechanism on the human evaluation side. The present estimation method is based on an expansion form of the Baye's theorem, and any kinds of statistics can be estimated. The effectiveness of the theory has been confirmed by application to room acoustics data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Guaranteed robust control of unstable systems by using approximated models
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: Some preliminary results regarding the design of low-order compensators for unstable plants are presented. With the proposed approach it is possible to compute the compensator which robustly stabilizes a given unstable plant, after approximating the system with a reduced-order model whose only constraint is retaining the same number of unstable poles as the original one. The conditions for obtaining a low order uncertainty function are also given. The solution to the problem can be obtained by using a min-max approximation approach. The proposed strategy is illustrated by a numerical example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data integration in multi-sensor based robotic workstations
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A relaxation labeling algorithm is developed for image processing and object identification. The major advantage of this algorithm over the existing one is that the mathematic operation is simplified. The simplification eases the analysis of the convergence properties. Both the theoretical and application aspects of the proposed algorithm are investigated. The local convergence properties of a labeling process with n labels and m labels are established. The investigation of the interaction among the nodes in a multinode labeling process reveals some insight into the mathematical issues involved in the relaxation operations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An extension of the Kiefer-Wolfowitz stochastic approximation procedure
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The Kiefer-Wolfowitz stochastic approximation procedure is utilized to find a maximum or a minimum point of a regression function. In the present work, an algorithm that is an extension of the usual Kiefer-Wolfowitz stochastic approximation procedure is proposed. The algorithm corresponds to an adaptive version of the usual Kiefer-Wolfowitz stochastic approximation procedure. The convergence of this algorithm is proved. The proposed algorithm has a faster convergence rate than the usual Kiefer-Wolfowitz procedure. A numerical simulation is shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Formulation of planning of vision and motion for a mobile robot under uncertainty
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A formulation for planning of vision and motion for a mobile robot under uncertainty is described. For planning in the real world, uncertainty and the cost of visual recognition are important issues. A robot has to consider a tradeoff between the cost of visual recognition and the effect of information obtained by recognition. One problem is to generate a sequence of vision and motion operations based on sensor information which is an integration of the current information and the predicted next sensor data. The problem is formulated by using statistical decision theory. A solution is obtained by recursive prediction of sensor information and the recursive search of operations. Using the framework, a robot can successfully generate a vision-motion plan.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Convolutional code and hybrid ARQ
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: Hybrid automatic repeat request (ARQ) combined with the convolutional code is considered, and it is shown how one can realize reliable transmission near the computational cutoff rate. Particular attention is given to a hybrid ARQ and burst trapping scheme for error detection. Some results of simulation over the additive white Gaussian noise channel are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multirate-PDA tracker
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A methodology for the use of the multirate sampling technique in the measurement acquisition process of a probabilistic data association (PDA) filter is presented. The proposed filter, called the multirate sample probabilistic data association (MSPDA) filter, increases the computational efficiency of the tracking system without compromising the accuracy of the tracking algorithm. The use of multirate sampling enhances the utilization of the central processor, since the time spent in acquiring and processing certain measurements relevant to the components of a state vector is considerably saved. The performance of the MSPDA filter is compared with that of the traditional PDA tracker and other presently used filters. It is shown that the computational saving is about 25% while the degradation in accuracy is only to the extent of 5% of the MSE of the corresponding state vector component.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive combination of equalization and decoding of error-correcting codes
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A combined technique of equalization and decoding of an error-correcting code is introduced. It is very useful for achieving highly reliable communications in channels corrupted by noise and intersymbol interference, such as a telephone subscriber channel and a mobile communications channel. Two types of structures and algorithms for combined equalization and decoding are presented. Equalization can achieve stable adaptation for unknown characteristics and/or variance of a channel by using some information obtained in decoding, while decoding can be modified to adapt to the condition of a channel by exploiting information from equalization. In particular, a method to utilize the reliability of decoded data for equalization and an adaptive decoding scheme based on the combined decoding and equalization are proposed. Theoretical error probability and simulation results are given to evaluate the communication system using the combined technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient algorithm for minimal partial realization of matrix sequences
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: An efficient algorithm for minimal partial realization of matrix sequences is presented. It is more efficient than any similar known algorithm based on matrix computations. At each iteration, one can update each current solution vector by a simple three-term recurrence instead of by a nonexplicit linear combination of auxiliary vectors. The proposed algorithm is a refinement of the Dickinson-Morf-Kailath algorithm (1974).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a parameterized fuzzy processor and its applications
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: The design of a parameterized fuzzy processor (PFP) which plays the role of a man-machine interface is described. The set of instructions is designed for supporting the versatility of the fuzzy information. The architecture of the PFP is also presented. Then, some applications of human inference and intuitive control are presented which show that the PFP is feasible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Designs of new smoothers for stationary systems and their implementations to third order electric circuit
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: A smoothing technology that is able to estimate original stationary signals or states of systems more accurately from the measured noisy signals or states based on a filtering process that is considered as an inverse system in the noisy environment is described. The noise treated is white Gaussian. The signals are various artificial voices, types of music, and moving pictures in robots. The part of the software that will be implemented in a special device is introduced, and results obtained are shown, including an explanation of a method of how to implement smoothing technologies by artificial neural networks or neurochips.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computational strategies for synthetic aperture imaging
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image reconstruction based on a convolution backpropagation (CBP) algorithm is discussed. The authors describe how the CBP algorithm can be modified and applied within the framework of constraints imposed by narrowband spotlight-mode SAR. With this approach, it is possible to begin producing the image as soon as the first return (projection) is recorded. An important advantage is that only 1-D interpolation is required, as compared to 2-D interpolation that is required with direct Fourier methods. Also, it is easy to produce a partial spatial domain image if it is determined part way through the processing that all targets of interest lie in a subregion of the image plane, or to produce a reduced resolution image while saving computation. The CBP SAR processing algorithm is demonstrated on real SAR images consisting of corner reflectors, and the resulting images are compared with equivalent Fourier domain reconstruction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reconstruction of CSG solid from a set of orthographic three views
publicationTitle: [Proceedings 1992] IEEE International Conference on Systems Engineering
abstract: An interpretation method of orthographic three-views of a mechanical drawing based on dividing operations into primitive volumes is presented. The method outputs a constructive solid geometry (CSG) solid model composed of a binary tree of direct sum and difference operations for object shapes limited to combinations of six primitives. The main parts of the method are to extract all loops, to obtain the combinations of the loops of 2-D primitives for each view, to generate all possible combinations of 3-D primitives, and to generate a CSG tree of the direct sum and difference operations on them. The algorithm is described, and some examples are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
